items.title: AI watermarking has a decentralisation problem
items.summary: With AI watermarking inference providers mark their output as AI generated. But for the system to become useful, lots of independent providers need to collaborate together in a decentralised system without overarching governance.

items.title: The Algorithm, Singular
items.summary: A new European ruling on algorithmic amplification determines if an operator controls how content spreads on a platform. But applying it to open social networks turns out to be a problem.

items.title: FR#168 – LLMs Join The Fediverse
items.summary: How to build a fediverse community when bots are indistinguishable from humans on applications to join?

items.title: The Permission Machine
items.summary: When Elon Musk calls to imprison the government, it turns out not to matter very much. But when thousands of accounts repeat each other, it matters enormously.

items.title: Decrypting Matrix – Where Do Rooms Go?
items.summary: Matrix has been running private rooms on open protocols for a decade, and they ended up inside European governments. This piece is about why happened, and why it does not have to be the result of the various projects for private data and rooms on the open social web too.

items.title: FR#166 – No Change
items.summary: Many people in Europe see the open social web as a path to digital sovereignty. This week demonstrated a problem: the assumption that European governments actually want to be sovereign.
